body:
Redline round 1

Reviewed the whole pull request.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 3d23086 returned 22 candidates: 19 verified, 1 could not be confirmed, 1 refuted, 0 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 1 already tracked.

This pull request moves every decision from the verifier to the shaper. The done rule, the review body, the handoff and the two overrule doors now follow that model, and the loop, gh and setup harnesses grow for each slice. Most findings sit where the new model meets the old. Some texts still state the old rule next to the new one: the v3 section's ask reasons, the unconditional never-re-raise sentence, and the final nit pass's scope against FACTS_ONLY. The correctness-only scope now keeps its declined items in the round, which shows in the findings file, the closing sentence and carried threads. The done rule treats a round with no fix commit as one that changed nothing, even when a standards commit landed. The repository has no scheduled or queued work. The version is bumped to 0.3.0, and every touched file has a Docs entry.

### Correctness (7)

- **R1-1** · correctness · low · confirmed · `agents/redline-reviewer.md:22` · The unconditional 'declined is not raised again' sentence contradicts the new decline-reopen rule
- **R1-8** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1365` · Final nit pass prompt ends with FACTS_ONLY, which contradicts its own scope line
- **R1-10** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2421` · Scope-declined items land in round-N-findings.json unmarked, so a revise of that round shapes them
- **R1-11** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2514` · A decline reason is posted raw in the handoff, so a bare @-word in it notifies an account
- **R1-12** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2579` · A v3 unattended section tells the shaper to ask with reasons checkCalls now rejects
- **R1-15** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3193` · The overrule instruction does not work for a declined finding in the review body
- **R1-20** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3816` · A round counts as changing no code when its only change is a standards commit

### Other items (12)

- **R1-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:362` · prior-findings leaves a 'left to the author under rule' tail in the title
- **R1-4** · nit · low · confirmed · `skills/redline/SKILL.md:97` · Skill text still lists needsDecision and leaves declined out of the tracked dispositions
- **R1-5** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:650` · One why_human enum for both pass kinds lets a Redline round's shaper return a reason that stops the run
- **R1-6** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:960` · Closing sentence promises a comment and reply for scope-declined items, which get neither
- **R1-7** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:973` · personLine is named for the removed For the person list
- **R1-9** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1815` · The pass-kind switch between NEVER_DECIDE and NOT_YOURS is written five times
- **R1-13** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2811` · checkCalls rejects a rule-covered call's reason before forceAskRules would overwrite it
- **R1-14** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3116` · The final-nit-pass found/fixed wording is written twice
- **R1-16** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3198` · The scope-declined line format is written twice
- **R1-17** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3306` · With no login, the cap-hit comment starts a sentence in lowercase
- **R1-18** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3730` · The 'out of scope (correctness only)' branch in earlierRoundsLines can no longer be reached
- **R1-19** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3742` · A carried nit declined under the scope gets no earlier-thread reply and is reported as 'not settled'

### Could not confirm (1)

- **R1-2** · nit · low · unconfirmed · `docs/running.md:116` · Docs say an overruled decline's thread stays open, though Finish already resolved it
  Would confirm it: Reply in a resolved review thread on a scratch pull request, then read its resolved state with `redline-gh.sh threads`.

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

### Candidates set aside (2)

<details>
<summary>Refuted, collapsed or already tracked</summary>

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:1506` · accountCoverage mints a new unconfirmed correctness finding for any entry whose outcome word is unknown, even when its ref names a finding of this round, so a habitual or older outcome word duplicates the finding. · refuted: Claim: the verifier returns an older outcome word such as 'finding' or 'forThePerson', and accountCoverage mints a duplicate finding from it. Evidence: REVIEW_SCHEMA limits coverage[].outcome to the COVERAGE_OUTCOMES enum (workflows/redline-loop.js:565, 578 and 590), and the structured-output tool validates that before the workflow reads the result. A real reviewer's unknown word never reaches the branch at line 1506; only a mock that skips the schema does.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:894` · Already tracked in #88 (a newline in posted free text can forge a line). What #88 is missing: the new `wouldConfirm` field is posted through postedText with no single-line step, unlike a minted title. · known: #88: its newline rule covers every posted free-text field, wouldConfirm included. The reviewer's own titles are not made single-line either, so the new field adds no case the issue leaves out.

</details>

comments.body:
**R1-1** · correctness · low · confirmed

**The unconditional 'declined is not raised again' sentence contradicts the new decline-reopen rule**

Line 22 still says, with no exception: 'A finding an earlier round declined, deferred or decided is not raised again.' The workflow's header for this run's earlier rounds says the same thing (`never re-raise a declined, deferred or decided one`, workflows/redline-loop.js:1330). This pull request adds a reopen rule two lines above (line 20) and in the candidates block (redline-loop.js:1402): a finding declined because it could not be confirmed, and that the verifier now confirms, is new. On a round-2 prompt both rules apply to the same item, since the history lists it with the outcome `declined: could not confirm: needs ...`. A verifier that follows the unconditional sentence keeps a confirmed correctness bug settled, and the run ends with it unfixed. Both sentences are unchanged context from the base, which had no decline-reopen rule, so the contradiction comes from this pull request.

Proposed fix: Qualify line 22 and the history header at redline-loop.js:1330 with the exception, for example 'is not raised again, except one declined because it could not be confirmed that you now confirm, as "What is new" says'. Pin the qualified phrase in the loop test's key-phrase checks.

**R1-2** · nit · low · unconfirmed

**Docs say an overruled decline's thread stays open, though Finish already resolved it**

Line 116 covers the overrule after a run: the person replies in the decline's thread and runs the human review pass. It ends: 'the thread stays open, since a person spoke in it.' But SETTLED_KINDS now includes `declined` (workflows/redline-loop.js:336), and threadCandidates marks a declined finding whose reply posted as settled (line 3390). So the original run's Finish sweep resolves that thread before the person can reply. A human review pass's own record is never a sweep candidate (line 3378), so nothing reopens it afterwards. The thread can stay open only if GitHub reopens a resolved thread when someone replies, and that is GitHub's behaviour, which the repository cannot show. Tried: traced the sweep and the human pass; did not test GitHub.

Proposed fix: Reword the sentence to say the run resolved the thread at its finish and the reply sits in that resolved thread. Alternatively, have the human review pass unresolve a thread it acts on.

Could not confirm. Would confirm it: Reply in a resolved review thread on a scratch pull request, then read its resolved state with `redline-gh.sh threads`.

**R1-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**prior-findings leaves a 'left to the author under rule' tail in the title**

The title pattern in prior-findings strips a rule tail in only three forms: `yours under rule`, `left to @<login> under rule` and `left to the person running Redline under rule`. findingLine (workflows/redline-loop.js:893) writes `left to ${personLabel} under rule <id>`. personLabel (line 190) is `the author` when no login is set and the run is a human review pass. The final nit pass after that pass is a Redline round whose body is built by findingLine, so a correctness finding under a repository rule posts `· left to the author under rule x`. The pattern misses it, the lazy title capture takes in the tail, and a later run's reviewer prompt and the handoff's Earlier rounds line show it as part of the title. Conditions: no login (the skill normally sets one from `redline-gh.sh login`), a human review pass, and a final-nit-pass finding under an ask rule. The candidate's second case, a `name[bot]` login, cannot happen: `redline-gh.sh login` reads `gh api user`, and user logins hold only letters, digits and hyphens. Replies are read correctly, since classify matches `startswith("left to the author")` (line 354).

Proposed fix: Add `the author` to the rule-tail alternatives at line 362, or have findingLine use the Redline-round fallback wording. Add a gh-test case for that line.

**R1-4** · nit · low · confirmed

**Skill text still lists needsDecision and leaves declined out of the tracked dispositions**

Line 190 still lists `needsDecision` among the fields of each finding in the `reviewed` hand-off. review() deletes that field from every finding (workflows/redline-loop.js:2271), and FINDING_SCHEMA no longer has it. Step 9 (line 97) lists the tracked dispositions as fixed, deferred, decided, dropped, carried or left, and leaves out `declined`. prior-findings now returns `declined` (scripts/redline-gh.sh:350), and the workflow treats it as tracked (PRIOR_DISPOSITIONS, redline-loop.js:86). Line 97 is a context line of the diff; line 190 is outside it.

Proposed fix: Remove `needsDecision` from the field list at line 190 and add `declined` to step 9's list of tracked dispositions.

**R1-5** · nit · low · confirmed

**One why_human enum for both pass kinds lets a Redline round's shaper return a reason that stops the run**

JUDGMENT_CALL_SCHEMA's why_human enum is the union of ROUND_WHY and HUMAN_WHY, plus the rule reasons, and SHAPE_SCHEMA is built once for both pass kinds. So `unsure`, `new standard` and `disproportionate fix` pass the structured-output check on a Redline round, and checkCalls then throws a shape-stage error (lines 2579-2581). The result is a stopped round and a resume. With an enum built per pass, the structured-output tool would reject the value and the shaper would retry inside the same agent run. This is the same stop as R1-12 and R1-13; a per-pass enum would turn each of them into a retry.

Proposed fix: Build the shape schema per pass. A Redline round's why_human enum is ROUND_WHY plus the rule reasons; a human review pass's is HUMAN_WHY plus the rule reasons. Keep checkCalls as the second layer.

**R1-6** · nit · low · confirmed

**Closing sentence promises a comment and reply for scope-declined items, which get neither**

Whenever `active` is not empty, reviewBody posts the closing sentence 'Each item has an inline comment ... Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker' (line 960). It comes after the scope-declined list (line 943). The items in that list have no inline comment and no marker, and they get no reply: they are left out of `active` (line 3731) and never shaped. This shows on any correctness-only round that has one active finding and one scope-declined item.

Proposed fix: Narrow the sentence, for example 'Each item above, except those declined under the scope, has an inline comment...'. Or move it before the scope-declined list.

**R1-7** · nit · low · confirmed

**personLine is named for the removed For the person list**

personLine (line 973) is now called only from setAsideBlock (line 1000). Its name comes from the For the person list that this pull request removes. Its comment was updated to describe a set-aside line, so only the name is stale, along with the mention at line 986.

Proposed fix: Rename it to setAsideLine, or inline it into setAsideBlock.

**R1-8** · correctness · low · confirmed

**Final nit pass prompt ends with FACTS_ONLY, which contradicts its own scope line**

Every review prompt now ends with FACTS_ONLY: 'Report every finding you verified, whatever its size, whatever its fix would cost and wherever its cause lies' (line 1365). The final nit pass prompt included. Four lines earlier, that same prompt says 'Report only correctness bugs introduced by this diff ... and do not report anything the diff did not introduce' (line 1361). A final nit pass has no candidates block (coverage is skipped there, line 2232), so nothing reconciles the two. If the reviewer follows the last instruction, a correctness bug in code the fixes did not touch passes the final pass's filter, which keeps every correctness finding (line 3720). It is then shaped and possibly fixed in a pass that is never re-reviewed. Conditions: a pre-existing correctness bug the reviewer notices during the final nit pass, and a reviewer that follows the closing sentence.

Proposed fix: On a final nit pass, leave FACTS_ONLY's 'wherever its cause lies' out. Alternatively, say in the final-nit-pass line that its scope overrides the sentence after it.

**R1-9** · nit · low · confirmed

**The pass-kind switch between NEVER_DECIDE and NOT_YOURS is written five times**

`pass.human ? NEVER_DECIDE : NOT_YOURS` appears as written in resolvePrompt (1702), standardsPrompt (1739) and implementPrompt (1815). planPrompt (1729) and reshapePrompt (1662, with ASK_CASES) use variants of it. All five are new in this pull request; the base used NEVER_DECIDE everywhere.

Proposed fix: Add a `decideRule(pass)` helper for the three uses that match exactly. The plan and reshape variants keep their own text.

**R1-10** · correctness · low · confirmed

**Scope-declined items land in round-N-findings.json unmarked, so a revise of that round shapes them**

Under correctness only, the scope-declined findings now stay in `considered` (lines 3717 and 3730-3731) and go to post() as `findings`. post() writes `findings: reviewOut.findings` into round-N-findings.json (line 2421) with no `scoped` key, so nothing marks them. `/redline:redline-revise <pr> round N` reads `findings` from that file (skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:15). The revise-only path then takes every finding without a knownAs as in scope (redline-loop.js:3687), so the items the run declined are shaped and can be fixed. Their replies go by the issue-comment route, behind a `<!-- redline:<id> -->` marker that no review body carries (replyEntry, line 1166), because a scope-declined line has no marker. Before #93, the base dropped these nits from `considered` before the file was written.

Proposed fix: Write the scope-declined ids into round-N-findings.json and have the revise-only path leave them out of inScope. Alternatively, keep them out of the file's `findings`, as before.

**R1-11** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A decline reason is posted raw in the handoff, so a bare @-word in it notifies an account**

#88 tracks reply text, which covers a decline reason in its thread reply, and lists the handoff's decision lines as outside its scope. What it does not cover: the handoff's '### Declined by Redline' lines post `- **<id>** <postedText(title)>: ${d.outcome}` (line 3182). That outcome is describeOutcome's `declined: ${outcome.reason}${owner}` (line 2514), which carries the shaper's free-text reason exactly as written. A reason holding a bare `@click` mentions the GitHub account `click`, and a bare tag such as `<Button>` is read as HTML. Decline reasons are new free text in this pull request and tend to quote code. The shaper's agent file asks for `@` identifiers in backticks, but that is an instruction, not a guarantee.

Proposed fix: Pass the decline's reason through postedText where the handoff posts it, keeping the `decided by` suffix as written. Add a loop check with `@click` and `<Button>` in a reason.

**R1-12** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**A v3 unattended section tells the shaper to ask with reasons checkCalls now rejects**

checkCalls now throws a shape-stage error for any Redline-round judgment call whose why_human is not in ROUND_WHY or a repository rule (lines 2579-2581). A repository whose unattended section is still v3 tells the shaper the opposite. Point 5 (templates/history/shape-spec-unattended.v3.md:52) says a finding it cannot confirm or refute is `ask` with `why_human: "unsure"`. The JSON example at line 70 lists `new standard | unsure | disproportionate fix`. The launch precheck only warns about an old marker (docs/upgrading.md:25), so plugin 0.3.0 runs against such a section until someone reruns `/redline:setup`. The shape prompt says to follow that section (line 1590). A resume reruns the same shaper over the same section. The stop needs the shaper to follow the section's point 5 over its agent file's rule 1, which is headed 'Rules that override everything else' and names only the new cases, and over the prompt's ASK_CASES. Before #93, checkCalls did not check why_human, so the same JSON went through.

Proposed fix: On a section whose marker is older than v4, accept HUMAN_WHY's reasons on a Redline round with a warning, or send `unsure` down the second-look path. Alternatively, make the precheck refuse a pre-v4 section instead of warning. Add a loop case with a v3 section.

**R1-13** · nit · low · confirmed

**checkCalls rejects a rule-covered call's reason before forceAskRules would overwrite it**

revise() runs checkCalls (line 2811) before forceAskRules (line 2813), and the reshape path does the same (2928, 2930). forceAskRules sets why_human to `repository rule <id>` for every finding a rule covers (lines 2674 and 2691). So if the shaper returns a rule-covered finding as ask with a reason outside the cases (`unsure`, `new standard`), the round stops at shape over a value the next line would have replaced. The shaper's documented promise is that the workflow forces `ask` 'whatever `fix`, `decline` or `defer` you return' (agents/redline-shaper.md:29), which covers the disposition only. Its rule 1 says the workflow stops on any other reason. Conditions: a finding under a repository rule, and a shaper that gives it a reason outside the cases.

Proposed fix: Skip the why_human test for a call on a finding that ruleForPaths, or a declared askRule tag, covers. Or run forceAskRules before that test.

**R1-14** · nit · low · confirmed

**The final-nit-pass found/fixed wording is written twice**

The three-way wording for a final nit pass (all fixed, none changed, some of each) is written in handoffComment (lines 3116-3123) and again in humanSummary (lines 3294-3298). These are two independent ternary chains with different sentences, both new in this pull request. They carry the rule that only an item a commit fixed is called fixed.

Proposed fix: Move the wording into one helper that takes (found, fixed) and a sentence style, and call it from both.

**R1-15** · correctness · low · confirmed

**The overrule instruction does not work for a declined finding in the review body**

The handoff says: to overrule a decline, 'reply in its thread, then run `/redline-revise <pr> review @<login>`' (line 3193; the same in docs/running.md:114 and the skill's closing summary). A finding GitHub could not anchor sits in the review body behind its marker and has no thread; its reply goes as an issue comment (replyEntry, line 1166). Since #93, a candidate whose cause is outside the diff keeps its own place and is moved into the body. `redline-gh.sh human-review` takes the person's open review comments and review bodies (scripts/redline-gh.sh:427-431). It reads issue comments only to find answered bodies (line 410). So a PR comment asking to fix such a finding is never picked up. The only route that works is a PR review with a body, which the instruction does not mention.

Proposed fix: Say in the overrule line that a finding with no thread is overruled by submitting a PR review whose body names it. Or teach human-review to read the person's issue comment that opens with the finding's marker.

**R1-16** · nit · low · confirmed

**The scope-declined line format is written twice**

The line `- ${f.id} · \`${f.file}:${f.line}\` · ${postedText(f.title)}` is written in reviewBody (line 943) and again in handoffComment (line 3198). Both depend on the id staying unbolded so that prior-findings never reads the line as a finding, and that rule now lives in two copies.

Proposed fix: Extract a `scopedLine(f)` helper and use it in both places.

**R1-17** · nit · low · confirmed

**With no login, the cap-hit comment starts a sentence in lowercase**

capComment writes `${personLabel} will pick these up.` at the start of a sentence (line 3306). With no login, personLabel is `the person running Redline` (line 190), so the posted comment reads '... so it has not requested a review. the person running Redline will pick these up.' The base wrote 'The author will pick these up.'

Proposed fix: Capitalise the fallback where it starts a sentence, for example with a `PersonLabel` variant: 'The person running Redline will pick these up.'

**R1-18** · nit · low · confirmed

**The 'out of scope (correctness only)' branch in earlierRoundsLines can no longer be reached**

earlierRoundsLines' `!ids.has(newId)` branch, 'carried forward as X, out of scope (correctness only)' (line 3442, outside the diff), ran when the correctness-only scope dropped a carried nit from `considered`. Since this pull request, scope-declined findings stay in record.findings (lines 3717 and 3730-3742). The run's first round is always `pr`, so `considered` is every finding the reviewer returned, and every carried id is among them. A scope-declined carried finding now goes through `record.outcomes[newId]` (SCOPE_DECLINED) instead. The cause is the scope change anchored here; the dead branch is at line 3442.

Proposed fix: Remove the `!ids.has(newId)` branch at line 3442.

**R1-19** · nit · low · confirmed

**A carried nit declined under the scope gets no earlier-thread reply and is reported as 'not settled'**

Under correctness only, an earlier round's undispositioned nit that the first round carries becomes a scope-declined finding. The record gives it `outcomes[newId] = SCOPE_DECLINED` but no outcomeKinds entry (line 3742). carriedReplies runs only over inScope (line 3069), and replyStandalone has no carried replies, so the earlier thread gets no reply. In the handoff, Earlier rounds says 'carried forward as R2-x: declined: outside this run's scope (correctness only)' (line 3445), and the item is listed under Declined under this run's scope. Meanwhile threadCandidates finds kinds[newId] empty and reports the earlier thread as '(not settled)' (lines 3408-3410). The next run's prior-findings sees no reply and carries it again. That matches the stated intent for scope-declined items (a later run without the scope sees them fresh, line 940), but the posted lines disagree about what happened to it.

Proposed fix: Give the earlier thread a reason that matches the handoff, for example 'declined under the scope', in threadCandidates. Or post a carried reply naming the scope decline.

**R1-20** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A round counts as changing no code when its only change is a standards commit**

fixedAny is `outcome.fixed.length > 0` (line 3816). `fixed` counts findings that a commit names (line 3090), and a lessons-only standards edit names no finding (implementPrompt, line 1812). Take a round whose findings are all declined and whose standards approver approves such an edit. The spec, standards and as-built commits are made and pushed (`doPush` when roundCommits is not empty, line 3070), but fixed is empty. With bought false, the run hands off: the standards change under agent-os/standards is never reviewed, and the result note says 'The last revise pass made no commits' (line 3822). That note is false for every revise pass that reaches implement, since a round always makes its spec commit (README, Git rules point 1). With bought true and coverage on, the next range carries `empty: true` (line 3826), and the prompt tells the reviewer that `git diff A..B -- ':/' ':(top,exclude)agent-os/specs'` 'is empty' (line 1306). That diff includes the standards edit, which the pathspec does not exclude. Before #93, any new head led to a fix-diff round or a final nit pass over it. The pull request's shape.md records 'the round's spec and standards commits are not one' as a shaping default (line 79), and plan.md:67 gives the reason as avoiding 'a final pass over an empty diff'. That reason does not hold when a standards edit lands.

Proposed fix: Set `empty` from the round's commits over the fix-diff pathspec, for example whether any round commit touches a path outside agent-os/specs (the checker's git block lists them). Reword the result note to 'committed no fix'.
